summary: Postinstall harvests environment variables and scans filesystem for credentials, exfiltrating to attacker-controlled ngrok tunnel
details: On npm install, the package's postinstall hook executes index.js, which POSTs the installer's full process.env, username, and current working directory to https://crabbing-thong-overhung.ngrok-free.dev/v1/init. It then spawns a detached background node process that recursively walks the entire filesystem from `/` (or `C:\` on Windows), reads files by extension (.env,.conf,.json,.yaml,.log, and similar), regex-matches JWT tokens and mongodb/postgres/mysql/redis/amqp connection URIs containing embedded credentials, and POSTs any matches together with the host name to /v1/leak on the same ngrok endpoint. Network transport uses plain HTTP. The package has no legitimate declared functionality corresponding to this behavior.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
